ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, given the quadratic function $y=-x^2+2x+m$ with its partial graph illustrated, what is the solution set of the quadratic inequality $-x^2+2x+m>0$ with respect to $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the graph, it is known that the axis of symmetry is the line $x=1$, \\
hence, the coordinate of the other intersection point of the quadratic function graph with the x-axis is $(-1, 0)$, \\
According to the graph: The range of $x$ for which the function value is greater than 0 is: $-1<x<3$, \\
therefore, the solution set for $-x^2+2x+m>0$ is $\boxed{-1<x<3}$.
